import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/test_3.csv"
]

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files[0], index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files[1], index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files[2], index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files[3], index_col=0)

# Transformation plan:
# - Target table has only one column: 'attributes' (string)
# - Source tables have the column 'attributes' but mostly NaN
# - The target examples show distinct attribute values like 'head_down', 'partial_obstruction', 'normal'
# - We need to extract all non-null 'attributes' values from all sources and combine them
# - Since many 'attributes' in sources are NaN, we filter them out
# - Union all non-null 'attributes' values from all sources
# - Remove duplicates to match target distinct attribute values
# - Reset index for clean output

# Extract non-null 'attributes' from each source
attrs_0 = df0['attributes'].dropna()
attrs_1 = df1['attributes'].dropna()
attrs_2 = df2['attributes'].dropna()
attrs_3 = df3['attributes'].dropna()

# Concatenate all attributes series
all_attrs = pd.concat([attrs_0, attrs_1, attrs_2, attrs_3], ignore_index=True)

# Drop duplicates and reset index
all_attrs_unique = all_attrs.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

# Create final DataFrame with target schema
target_df = pd.DataFrame({'attributes': all_attrs_unique.astype(str)})

# Save to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
